questions.skill: Use the theorem inside another figure
questions.stem: A rectangle has one side of 9 centimeters and a diagonal of 15 centimeters. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The other side squared = 15^2 - 9^2 = 225 - 81 = 144, so the other side is 12 cm. The perimeter is 2 x (9 + 12) = 42 centimeters.

questions.skill: Use the converse to test for a right triangle
questions.stem: Which set of side lengths forms a right triangle?
questions.solution: Check each set against a^2 + b^2 = c^2 with c the longest side. 9^2 + 12^2 = 81 + 144 = 225 = 15^2. The others fail: 36 + 49 = 85 (not 100), 49 + 64 = 113 (not 121), 25 + 64 = 89 (not 100).

questions.skill: Find a hypotenuse in a real-world problem
questions.stem: A park path goes 24 meters west and then 7 meters north. A shortcut goes straight from the start to the end. How many meters shorter is the shortcut than the two-part path?
questions.solution: The shortcut is the hypotenuse: 24^2 + 7^2 = 576 + 49 = 625, so it is 25 meters. The two-part path is 24 + 7 = 31 meters. The shortcut is 31 - 25 = 6 meters shorter.

questions.skill: Use the theorem inside another figure
questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 centimeters and one leg of 5 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The other leg squared = 13^2 - 5^2 = 169 - 25 = 144, so it is 12 cm. The legs are the base and height, so the area is 5 x 12 / 2 = 30 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Estimate a side length that is not a whole number
questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of 5 units and 7 units. The hypotenuse is between which two whole numbers?
questions.solution: Hypotenuse squared = 5^2 + 7^2 = 25 + 49 = 74. Since 8^2 = 64 and 9^2 = 81, and 74 is between them, the hypotenuse is between 8 and 9.

questions.skill: Find a leg in a real-world problem
questions.stem: A 25-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall on level ground with its base 7 feet from the wall. The top of the ladder slides down the wall 4 feet, and the ladder is still 25 feet long. How many feet farther from the wall is the base of the ladder now?
questions.solution: At first the ladder reaches sqrt(25^2 - 7^2) = sqrt(625 - 49) = 24 feet high. After sliding down 4 feet it reaches 20 feet. The base is then sqrt(625 - 400) = 15 feet from the wall, which is 15 - 7 = 8 feet farther.

solve.work: Height sqrt(625-49)=24; new height 20; new base sqrt(625-400)=15; 15-7=8.

questions.skill: Use the converse to test for a right triangle
questions.stem: A triangle has sides of 8 cm, 11 cm and 14 cm. Pita finds that $8^2 + 11^2 = 185$ and $14^2 = 196$. She says, "These are close, so it is a right triangle." Which statement is correct?
choices: It is not a right triangle, because 185 does not equal 196.
It is a right triangle, because 185 is close to 196.
It is a right triangle, because 14 is the longest side.
It is not a right triangle, because 8 + 11 is greater than 14.
questions.answer: It is not a right triangle, because 185 does not equal 196.
questions.solution: The converse of the Pythagorean Theorem needs the squares of the shorter sides to add up exactly to the square of the longest side. 185 is not equal to 196, so the triangle is not a right triangle, however close the numbers are.

solve.answer: It is not a right triangle, because 185 does not equal 196.

questions.skill: Use the theorem inside another figure
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has two sides of 10 centimeters and a base of 12 centimeters. The height from the top corner straight down to the base meets the base at its midpoint, at a right angle. How tall is the triangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The height splits the base into two parts of 6 cm and forms a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 cm and one leg 6 cm. Height squared = 10^2 - 6^2 = 100 - 36 = 64, so the height is 8 centimeters.

questions.skill: Use the theorem with an unknown length in algebra
questions.stem: One leg of a right triangle is 12 units long. The hypotenuse is 2 units longer than the other leg. How long is the hypotenuse, in units?
questions.solution: Let the other leg be a, so the hypotenuse is a + 2. Then 12^2 + a^2 = (a + 2)^2, so 144 + a^2 = a^2 + 4a + 4. This gives 140 = 4a, so a = 35 and the hypotenuse is 37. Check: 144 + 1225 = 1369 = 37^2.

questions.skill: Use the converse in a real-world problem
questions.stem: A triangle has sides of 90 cm, 1.2 m and 1.5 m. Is it a right triangle?
questions.solution: Use one unit for all sides: 1.2 m = 120 cm and 1.5 m = 150 cm. Then 90^2 + 120^2 = 8100 + 14400 = 22500 = 150^2, so it is a right triangle. Mixing centimeters and meters gives meaningless sums.

questions.skill: Use the theorem inside another figure
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 300 square centimeters and one side of 15 centimeters. How long is its diagonal, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The other side is 300 / 15 = 20 cm. The diagonal is the hypotenuse: 15^2 + 20^2 = 225 + 400 = 625, so the diagonal is 25 centimeters.

questions.skill: Use the theorem inside another figure
questions.stem: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 centimeters and 30 centimeters. They cross at right angles and cut each other in half, and all four sides are equal. How long is one side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Each side is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs are half of each diagonal: 8 cm and 15 cm. 8^2 + 15^2 = 64 + 225 = 289, so each side is 17 centimeters.

questions.skill: legs of the right triangle
questions.stem: Points $A(1, 2)$ and $B(4, 6)$ are on a coordinate grid. Draw a horizontal segment from $A$ and a vertical segment from $B$; they meet at $(4, 2)$ and make a right triangle with $\overline{AB}$ as the longest side. How long is the horizontal leg?
questions.solution: The horizontal leg runs from $x = 1$ to $x = 4$ along $y = 2$, so its length is $4 - 1 = 3$.

questions.skill: distance from a whole-number triple
questions.stem: On a coordinate grid, point $P$ is at $(0, 0)$ and point $Q$ is at $(3, 4)$. Use the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance from $P$ to $Q$.
questions.solution: The legs are 3 and 4. The distance is $\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{25} = 5$.

questions.skill: legs of the right triangle
questions.stem: To find the distance from $(2, 1)$ to $(7, 13)$, you make a right triangle with a horizontal leg and a vertical leg. What are the lengths of the two legs?
questions.solution: The horizontal leg is $7 - 2 = 5$ and the vertical leg is $13 - 1 = 12$.

questions.skill: distance from a whole-number triple
questions.stem: A drawing program places point $C$ at $(1, 1)$ and point $D$ at $(7, 9)$. How far apart are the points, in grid units?
questions.solution: The legs are $7 - 1 = 6$ and $9 - 1 = 8$. The distance is $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{100} = 10$.

questions.skill: distance from a whole-number triple
questions.stem: What is the distance from $(0, 0)$ to $(5, 12)$?
questions.solution: The legs are 5 and 12. The distance is $\sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{169} = 13$. Adding the legs gives 17, subtracting gives 7, and 169 is the distance squared.

questions.skill: squared distance
questions.stem: Point $M$ is at $(0, 0)$ and point $N$ is at $(2, 5)$. What is the square of the distance from $M$ to $N$?
questions.solution: By the Pythagorean Theorem, $d^2 = 2^2 + 5^2 = 4 + 25 = 29$.

questions.skill: distance as a square root
questions.stem: What is the distance from $(0, 0)$ to $(3, 1)$?
questions.solution: The legs are 3 and 1, so $d = \sqrt{3^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{10}$. Adding the legs gives 4, and 10 is the distance squared.

questions.skill: distance in context
questions.stem: A robot starts at the origin of a grid and drives in a straight line to the point $(9, 12)$. Each grid unit is 1 meter. How far does it drive?
questions.solution: The legs are 9 and 12, so the distance is $\sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{225} = 15$ meters.

questions.skill: setting up the distance equation
questions.stem: Which equation can be used to find the distance $d$ between $(1, 2)$ and $(4, 6)$?
questions.solution: The horizontal change is $4 - 1 = 3$ and the vertical change is $6 - 2 = 4$. These are the legs, so $d^2 = 3^2 + 4^2$.

questions.skill: legs of the right triangle
questions.stem: Point $A$ is at $(-3, 0)$ and point $B$ is at $(0, 4)$. What is the distance from $A$ to $B$?
questions.solution: The horizontal leg is $0 - (-3) = 3$ and the vertical leg is $4 - 0 = 4$. The distance is $\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$.

questions.skill: distance from a whole-number triple
questions.stem: Find the distance between $(-4, -2)$ and $(4, 13)$.
questions.solution: The horizontal leg is $4 - (-4) = 8$ and the vertical leg is $13 - (-2) = 15$. The distance is $\sqrt{8^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{289} = 17$.

questions.skill: distance as a square root
questions.stem: What is the distance between $(1, 2)$ and $(4, 8)$?
questions.solution: The legs are $4 - 1 = 3$ and $8 - 2 = 6$, so $d = \sqrt{3^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{45}$. Multiplying the legs gives 18, subtracting the squares gives 27, and adding the legs gives 9.

questions.skill: distance in context
questions.stem: On a town map, each grid unit is 1 kilometer. The library is at $(2, 3)$ and the park is at $(10, 18)$. How far apart are they in a straight line?
questions.solution: The legs are $10 - 2 = 8$ and $18 - 3 = 15$. The distance is $\sqrt{8^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{289} = 17$ kilometers.

questions.skill: comparing distances
questions.stem: Which point is exactly 10 units from the origin $(0, 0)$?
questions.solution: For $(6, 8)$, $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{100} = 10$. The points $(5, 5)$ and $(7, 3)$ have coordinates that add to 10 but are not 10 units away, and $(10, 10)$ is about 14.1 units away.

questions.skill: perimeter on the grid
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(6, 0)$ and $(6, 8)$. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: The sides along the grid lines are 6 and 8. The third side is $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10$. The perimeter is $6 + 8 + 10 = 24$.

questions.skill: distance from a whole-number triple
questions.stem: Find the distance between $(-5, -7)$ and $(7, 2)$.
questions.solution: The legs are $7 - (-5) = 12$ and $2 - (-7) = 9$. The distance is $\sqrt{12^2 + 9^2} = \sqrt{225} = 15$.

questions.skill: distance from a whole-number triple
questions.stem: Point $A$ is at $(-3, 4)$ and point $B$ is at $(2, -8)$. What is the length of $\overline{AB}$?
questions.solution: The legs are $2 - (-3) = 5$ and $4 - (-8) = 12$. The length is $\sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = 13$. Adding the legs gives 17, and subtracting 12 and 5 gives 7.

questions.skill: comparing distances
questions.stem: Which of these points is farthest from the origin $(0, 0)$?
questions.solution: Compare the squared distances: $(2, 8)$ gives 68, $(3, 7)$ gives 58, $(5, 5)$ gives 50 and $(6, 4)$ gives 52. The largest is 68, so $(2, 8)$ is farthest.

questions.skill: squared distance
questions.stem: What is the square of the distance between $(-1, 4)$ and $(5, -2)$?

questions.skill: distance in context
questions.stem: A drone takes off at the point $(0, 0)$ of a map grid and flies in a straight line to the point $(24, 7)$. One grid unit is 1 kilometer. How many kilometers does it fly?
questions.solution: The legs are 24 and 7. The distance is $\sqrt{24^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{625} = 25$ kilometers.

questions.skill: missing coordinate from a distance
questions.stem: The distance from the origin $(0, 0)$ to the point $(k, 12)$ is 13 units, and $k$ is positive. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The legs are $k$ and 12 and the longest side is 13, so $k^2 + 12^2 = 13^2$. Then $k^2 = 169 - 144 = 25$ and $k = 5$.

questions.skill: missing coordinate from a distance
questions.stem: The point $(x, 11)$ is 10 units from the point $(2, 3)$, and $x$ is greater than 2. What is $x$?
questions.solution: The vertical leg is $11 - 3 = 8$. With distance 10, the horizontal leg is $\sqrt{10^2 - 8^2} = 6$. So $x = 2 + 6 = 8$.

solve.work: Vertical leg 8, so horizontal leg sqrt(100-64) = 6; x = 2 + 6 = 8.

questions.skill: perimeter on the grid
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices $A(0, 0)$, $B(4, 3)$ and $C(8, 0)$. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: $AB = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5$. $BC$ has legs $8 - 4 = 4$ and 3, so $BC = 5$. $AC$ lies along the $x$-axis and has length 8. The perimeter is $5 + 5 + 8 = 18$.

solve.work: AB = sqrt(16+9) = 5, BC = sqrt(16+9) = 5, AC = 8; perimeter 18.

questions.skill: right triangle test on the grid
questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(1, 1)$, $B(5, 4)$ and $C(8, 0)$. Which statement is true?
choices: It is a right triangle, because $AB + BC = AC$.
It is not a right triangle, because $AB^2 + BC^2 \ne AC^2$.
It is a right triangle, because $AB^2 + BC^2 = AC^2$.
It is not a right triangle, because no two sides are equal.
questions.answer: It is a right triangle, because $AB^2 + BC^2 = AC^2$.
questions.solution: $AB^2 = 4^2 + 3^2 = 25$, $BC^2 = 3^2 + 4^2 = 25$ and $AC^2 = 7^2 + 1^2 = 50$. Since $25 + 25 = 50$, the Pythagorean Theorem holds and the angle at $B$ is a right angle.

solve.answer: It is a right triangle, because $AB^2 + BC^2 = AC^2$.
solve.work: AB^2 = 16+9 = 25, BC^2 = 9+16 = 25, AC^2 = 49+1 = 50. 25+25 = 50, so right angle at B. (Option B is also false: AB = BC.)

questions.skill: diagonal of a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangle has corners at $(-3, -2)$, $(5, -2)$, $(5, 13)$ and $(-3, 13)$. How long is a diagonal of the rectangle?
questions.solution: The width is $5 - (-3) = 8$ and the height is $13 - (-2) = 15$. The diagonal is the longest side of a right triangle with these legs: $\sqrt{8^2 + 15^2} = 17$.

questions.skill: comparing distances
questions.stem: Which point is exactly 13 units from the point $(1, 2)$?
questions.solution: For $(6, 14)$ the legs are $6 - 1 = 5$ and $14 - 2 = 12$, and $\sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = 13$. The other points are $\sqrt{153}$, $\sqrt{89}$ and 10 units away.

questions.skill: distance in context
questions.stem: A hiker walks in a straight line from $(0, 0)$ to $(5, 12)$, then in a straight line from $(5, 12)$ to $(14, 24)$. Each grid unit is 1 kilometer. How far does the hiker walk in all?
questions.solution: The first part is $\sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = 13$. The second part has legs $14 - 5 = 9$ and $24 - 12 = 12$, so it is $\sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = 15$. The total is $13 + 15 = 28$ kilometers.

solve.work: First leg sqrt(25+144) = 13; second legs 9 and 12, sqrt(81+144) = 15; total 28 km.

questions.skill: distance as a square root
questions.stem: What is the distance between $(-2, 5)$ and $(3, -1)$?
questions.solution: The legs are $3 - (-2) = 5$ and $5 - (-1) = 6$, so $d = \sqrt{5^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{61}$. Subtracting $-2$ as if it were $+2$ gives $\sqrt{17}$, and adding the legs gives 11.

questions.skill: comparing distances
questions.stem: Walking from $P(1, 1)$ to $Q(7, 9)$ along grid lines (across, then up) is an L-shaped path. How many units shorter is the straight line from $P$ to $Q$ than that L-shaped path?
questions.solution: The L-shaped path is $(7 - 1) + (9 - 1) = 6 + 8 = 14$ units. The straight line is $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10$ units. The difference is $14 - 10 = 4$.

questions.skill: distance in context
questions.stem: In a game, a character stands at the pixel position $(40, 30)$ and a target is at $(160, 190)$. One grid unit is one pixel. How far is the target from the character?
questions.solution: The legs are $160 - 40 = 120$ and $190 - 30 = 160$. The distance is $\sqrt{120^2 + 160^2} = \sqrt{40000} = 200$ pixels.

questions.skill: volume of a cylinder
questions.stem: A can is a cylinder with a radius of 3 centimeters and a height of 10 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the volume of the can, in cubic centimeters?

questions.skill: volume of a cone
questions.stem: A cone has a radius of 3 inches and a height of 4 inches. What is the volume of the cone, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (9)(4) = 12\pi$. Leaving out the $\frac{1}{3}$ gives $36\pi$, not squaring the radius gives $4\pi$, and swapping the radius and height gives $16\pi$.

questions.skill: volume of a sphere
questions.stem: A sphere has a radius of 3 inches. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the volume of the sphere, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times 3.14 \times 27 = 4 \times 3.14 \times 9 = 113.04$.

questions.skill: relating the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres
questions.stem: A cone and a cylinder have the same base and the same height. The volume of the cylinder is 54 cubic inches. What is the volume of the cone, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: The volume of a cone is one third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height: $54 \div 3 = 18$.

questions.skill: relating the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres
questions.stem: Which formula gives the volume of a sphere with radius $r$?
questions.solution: The volume of a sphere is $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$. The formula $4\pi r^2$ is the surface area, not the volume.

questions.skill: volume of a sphere
questions.stem: A sphere has a radius of 6 centimeters. What is the volume of the sphere, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (216) = 288\pi$. Using $4\pi r^2$ gives $144\pi$, leaving out the $\frac{4}{3}$ gives $864\pi$, and using the cone formula gives $72\pi$.

questions.skill: volume of a cone
questions.stem: A cone has a radius of 3 centimeters and a height of 10 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the volume of the cone, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times 3.14 \times 9 \times 10 = 3.14 \times 30 = 94.2$.

questions.skill: volume of a cylinder
questions.stem: A cylinder has a radius of 4 feet and a height of 3 feet. What is the volume of the cylinder, in cubic feet?
questions.solution: $V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (16)(3) = 48\pi$. The value $24\pi$ comes from $2\pi r h$ and $12\pi$ from forgetting to square the radius.

questions.skill: volume of a cylinder
questions.stem: A cylinder has a base with an area of 12 square centimeters and a height of 7 centimeters. What is the volume of the cylinder, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The volume of a cylinder is the area of the base times the height: $12 \times 7 = 84$.

questions.skill: relating the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres
questions.stem: A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and the same height. Which statement is true?
choices: The volume of the cone is one half of the volume of the cylinder.
The volume of the cone is three times the volume of the cylinder.
The volume of the cone is equal to the volume of the cylinder.
The volume of the cone is one third of the volume of the cylinder.
questions.answer: The volume of the cone is one third of the volume of the cylinder.
questions.solution: The cone has $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$ and the cylinder has $\pi r^2 h$, so the cone is one third of the cylinder.

solve.answer: The volume of the cone is one third of the volume of the cylinder.
solve.work: Cone volume (1/3) pi r^2 h, cylinder pi r^2 h: one third.

questions.skill: volume of a cylinder
questions.stem: A cylindrical water bottle has a diameter of 8 inches and a height of 5 inches. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the volume of the bottle, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: The radius is half the diameter: 4 inches. $V = 3.14 \times 4^2 \times 5 = 3.14 \times 80 = 251.2$.

questions.skill: volume of a cone
questions.stem: A cone-shaped tent has a base with a diameter of 6 feet and a height of 9 feet. What is the volume of the tent, in cubic feet?
questions.solution: The radius is 3 feet. $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi (3^2)(9) = 27\pi$. Using 6 as the radius gives $108\pi$, and leaving out the $\frac{1}{3}$ gives $81\pi$.

questions.skill: finding a missing dimension from a volume
questions.stem: A cylinder has a volume of 314 cubic centimeters and a radius of 5 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the height of the cylinder, in centimeters?

questions.skill: volume of a sphere
questions.stem: A sphere has a diameter of 10 centimeters. What is the volume of the sphere, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The radius is 5 centimeters. $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi (125) = \frac{500}{3}\pi$. Using 10 as the radius gives $\frac{4000}{3}\pi$.

questions.skill: relating the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres
questions.stem: A cone-shaped paper cup and a cylinder-shaped glass have the same radius and the same height. The cup holds 25 milliliters of water. How many milliliters does the glass hold?
questions.solution: The cone holds one third as much as the cylinder, so the glass holds $3 \times 25 = 75$ milliliters.

questions.skill: how volume changes when a dimension changes
questions.stem: The radius of a cylinder is doubled and its height stays the same. How does the volume of the cylinder change?
questions.solution: The radius is squared in $V = \pi r^2 h$, so doubling it multiplies the volume by $2^2 = 4$.

solve.work: pi (2r)^2 h = 4 pi r^2 h: 4 times.

questions.skill: finding a missing dimension from a volume
questions.stem: A cone has a volume of 100.48 cubic centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the radius of the cone, in centimeters?

questions.skill: volume of a cone
questions.stem: An ice cream cone is a cone with a radius of 6 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $V = \frac{1}{3} \times 3.14 \times 6^2 \times 5 = 3.14 \times 60 = 188.4$. Leaving out the $\frac{1}{3}$ gives 565.2, using the diameter as the radius gives 753.6, and not squaring the radius gives 31.4.

questions.skill: relating the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres
questions.stem: A sphere fits exactly inside a cylinder: it touches the top, the bottom and the side of the cylinder. The volume of the cylinder is 162 cubic centimeters. What is the volume of the sphere, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: If the sphere has radius $r$, the cylinder has radius $r$ and height $2r$. The cylinder is $2\pi r^3$ and the sphere is $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$, which is $\frac{2}{3}$ of the cylinder: $\frac{2}{3} \times 162 = 108$.

solve.work: Cylinder r, height 2r: 2 pi r^3; sphere (4/3) pi r^3 = 2/3 of cylinder; 162 x 2/3 = 108.

questions.skill: volume of a cylinder
questions.stem: A cylindrical tank has a diameter of 6 meters and a height of 5 meters. What is the volume of the tank, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: The radius is 3 meters. $V = \pi (9)(5) = 45\pi$. Using the diameter as the radius gives $180\pi$, and $30\pi$ comes from $2\pi r h$.

questions.skill: volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: An ice cream cone is a cone with a radius of 3 centimeters and a height of 9 centimeters. A scoop of ice cream in the shape of a half sphere (a hemisphere) with the same radius sits on top of the cone. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the total volume of the cone and the scoop, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Cone: $\frac{1}{3} \times 3.14 \times 9 \times 9 = 3.14 \times 27 = 84.78$. Half sphere: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3} \times 3.14 \times 27 = 3.14 \times 18 = 56.52$. Total: $84.78 + 56.52 = 141.3$.

questions.skill: volume carried from one solid to another
questions.stem: A cone-shaped cup has a radius of 6 centimeters and a height of 9 centimeters. It is filled with water, and all of the water is poured into a cylinder with a radius of 3 centimeters. How deep is the water in the cylinder, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The cup holds $\frac{1}{3}\pi (36)(9) = 108\pi$. In the cylinder, $\pi (9) h = 108\pi$, so $h = 12$.

solve.work: Cone (1/3) pi 36 x 9 = 108 pi; pi x 9 x h = 108 pi, h = 12.

questions.skill: how volume changes when a dimension changes
questions.stem: Sphere A has a radius of 2 centimeters and Sphere B has a radius of 6 centimeters. The volume of Sphere B is how many times the volume of Sphere A?
questions.solution: The radius is 3 times as large, and volume depends on the cube of the radius, so the volume is $3^3 = 27$ times as large. The value 3 uses the radius ratio only, 9 squares it, and 4 subtracts the radii.

questions.skill: finding a missing dimension from a volume
questions.stem: A sphere has a volume of $\frac{256}{3}\pi$ cubic centimeters. What is the radius of the sphere, in centimeters?

questions.skill: relating the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres
questions.stem: A cone and a cylinder have the same height. The radius of the cone is twice the radius of the cylinder. The volume of the cone is how many times the volume of the cylinder?
questions.solution: With radius $r$ for the cylinder, its volume is $\pi r^2 h$. The cone has $\frac{1}{3}\pi (2r)^2 h = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^2 h$, which is $\frac{4}{3}$ of the cylinder.

solve.work: Cone (1/3) pi (2r)^2 h = (4/3) pi r^2 h vs cylinder pi r^2 h: 4/3.

questions.skill: volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: A capsule has a straight part shaped like a cylinder with a radius of 3 millimeters and a height of 8 millimeters. A half sphere with a radius of 3 millimeters is attached to each end. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the volume of the capsule, in cubic millimeters?
questions.solution: The two half spheres make one sphere: $\frac{4}{3} \times 3.14 \times 27 = 113.04$. The cylinder is $3.14 \times 9 \times 8 = 226.08$. Total: $113.04 + 226.08 = 339.12$.

solve.work: Cylinder 3.14 x 9 x 8 = 226.08; two hemispheres = sphere (4/3)(3.14)(27) = 113.04; total 339.12.

questions.skill: how volume changes when a dimension changes
questions.stem: A cone's radius is cut in half and its height is multiplied by 3. The volume of the new cone is how many times the volume of the original cone?
questions.solution: Halving the radius multiplies the volume by $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}$, and tripling the height multiplies it by 3, so the volume is $\frac{3}{4}$ of the original.

questions.skill: volume carried from one solid to another
questions.stem: A cylinder has a radius of 4 centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. A small cone has a radius of 2 centimeters and a height of 3 centimeters. How many full small cones of sand are needed to fill the cylinder?
questions.solution: The cylinder holds $\pi (16)(6) = 96\pi$. One small cone holds $\frac{1}{3}\pi (4)(3) = 4\pi$. Then $96\pi \div 4\pi = 24$ cones.

solve.work: Cylinder pi 16 x 6 = 96 pi; cone (1/3) pi 4 x 3 = 4 pi; 96/4 = 24.

questions.skill: volume carried from one solid to another
questions.stem: A solid metal sphere with a radius of 3 centimeters is melted and made into a solid cylinder with a radius of 3 centimeters. The volume does not change. What is the height of the cylinder, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The sphere has volume $\frac{4}{3}\pi (27) = 36\pi$. The cylinder has volume $\pi (9) h$. Setting $9\pi h = 36\pi$ gives $h = 4$.

solve.work: Sphere (4/3) pi 27 = 36 pi; 9 pi h = 36 pi, h = 4.

questions.skill: volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: What is the volume of a half sphere (a hemisphere) with a radius of 9 centimeters, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: A sphere with radius 9 has volume $\frac{4}{3}\pi (729) = 972\pi$, and half of it is $486\pi$. Forgetting to halve gives $972\pi$, using the cone formula gives $243\pi$, and using $\frac{2}{3}\pi r^2$ gives $54\pi$.

questions.skill: Find the equation of a line drawn through two points
questions.stem: A line of best fit is drawn through the points $(2, 7)$ and $(8, 10)$. Which equation does it have?
questions.solution: The slope is $(10 - 7) \div (8 - 2) = \frac{1}{2}$. Then $7 = \frac{1}{2}(2) + b$, so $b = 6$. The equation is $y = \frac{1}{2}x + 6$.

questions.skill: Judge how well a line fits
questions.stem: Nine points lie close to the line $y = x + 1$, and a tenth lies far above it. A student redraws the line so that it passes through the far point too. What happens to the nine points?
choices: Most of them end up farther from the line than before.
They all end up closer to the line than before.
They stay just as close to the line as before.
All nine end up exactly on the new line.
questions.answer: Most of them end up farther from the line than before.
questions.solution: The new line is tilted or lifted toward the far point. That moves it away from the nine points that already followed a pattern, so most are farther from it.

solve.answer: Most of them end up farther from the line than before.
solve.work: Tilting/moving the line to reach a far outlier pulls it away from the nine nearby points, so most end up farther away.

questions.skill: Compare two lines for fit
questions.stem: Two lines are tried on six points. From Line A the points are 2 above, 2 below, 1 above, 1 below, 2 above and 2 below. From Line B all six points are above the line, by 3, 3, 4, 2, 3 and 4 units. Which line fits better?
choices: Line B, because all of its points lie on the same side.
Line B, because its distances add to a greater total.
Line A, because its points are nearer and fall on both sides.
Both fit equally well, because each has six points.
questions.answer: Line A, because its points are nearer and fall on both sides.
questions.solution: Line A has smaller distances, and its points are on both sides of it. Line B is too low: every point is above it and farther away. So Line A fits better.

solve.answer: Line A, because its points are nearer and fall on both sides.
solve.work: Line A: distances 2,2,1,1,2,2 (total 10) on both sides. Line B: 3,3,4,2,3,4 (total 19), all above. Line A fits better.

questions.skill: Vertical distance of a point from a line
questions.stem: A line is $y = 1.5x + 2$. The data points are $(2, 6)$, $(4, 7)$, $(6, 14)$ and $(8, 12)$. How many units is the farthest point from the line, measured straight up or down?
questions.solution: The line has $y = 5, 8, 11, 14$ at $x = 2, 4, 6, 8$. The distances are $1, 1, 3, 2$. The farthest is 3 units, at $(6, 14)$.

solve.work: Line: x=2:5 (dist 1), x=4:8 (dist 1), x=6:11 (dist 3), x=8:14 (dist 2). Farthest 3.

questions.skill: Use a fitted line for an estimate
questions.stem: A line of best fit for a cocoa stand is $y = -3x + 100$, where $x$ is the temperature in degrees and $y$ is the cups sold. At what temperature does the line predict 46 cups?
questions.solution: Set $-3x + 100 = 46$. Then $-3x = -54$, so $x = 18$ degrees.

questions.skill: Decide when a straight line is a reasonable fit
questions.stem: A scatter plot has the points $(1, 3)$, $(2, 7)$, $(3, 9)$, $(4, 7)$ and $(5, 3)$. Why is a straight line a poor fit?
choices: The points are all at different heights, so no line can be drawn.
The points rise and then fall, so no single line stays near them.
The $x$-values are too small for a line to be drawn.
The points only fall, so a line would have to slope up.
questions.answer: The points rise and then fall, so no single line stays near them.
questions.solution: The points go up to $(3, 9)$ and then come back down. Any straight line is far from some of the points, so no line fits well.

solve.answer: The points rise and then fall, so no single line stays near them.
solve.work: y = 3,7,9,7,3 rise then fall; no single line stays near them.

questions.skill: Judge how well a line fits
questions.stem: Five points are all above the line $y = 2x + 1$, by 3, 2, 4, 3 and 3 units. A student moves the line up by 3 units to $y = 2x + 4$. What is the new total vertical distance of the five points from the line?
questions.solution: The new distances are $3 - 3 = 0$, $2 - 3 = -1$, $4 - 3 = 1$, $3 - 3 = 0$ and $3 - 3 = 0$. Ignoring signs, the total is $0 + 1 + 1 + 0 + 0 = 2$.

solve.work: Raising the line by 3 changes the distances to 0,1,1,0,0 (|3-3|,|2-3|,|4-3|,|3-3|,|3-3|). Total 2.

questions.skill: Predict with the model
questions.stem: A model for the height $h$, in centimeters, of a bean plant is $h = 2x + 5$, where $x$ is the number of weeks since planting. What height does the model predict after 6 weeks?
questions.solution: Put 6 in place of $x$: $2 \times 6 + 5 = 12 + 5 = 17$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope
questions.stem: The cost $y$, in dollars, of renting a bike for $x$ hours is modeled by $y = 3x + 10$. What does the 3 tell you?
choices: The rental has a starting charge of 3 dollars.
Each extra hour adds 3 dollars to the cost.
Each extra hour adds 10 dollars to the cost.
questions.answer: Each extra hour adds 3 dollars to the cost.
questions.solution: The number multiplying $x$ is the slope. It is the change in cost for each 1 hour more: 3 dollars per hour. The 10 is the cost at 0 hours.

solve.answer: Each extra hour adds 3 dollars to the cost.
solve.work: 3 is the slope: dollars per hour.

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept
questions.stem: A gym's total cost $y$, in dollars, after $x$ months is modeled by $y = 12x + 30$. What does the 30 tell you?
choices: The gym charges 30 dollars for every month.
After 30 months the total cost is 12 dollars.
The cost goes up 30 dollars every 12 months.
A one-time fee of 30 dollars is paid at the start.
questions.answer: A one-time fee of 30 dollars is paid at the start.
questions.solution: The constant is the intercept, the predicted cost when $x = 0$ months. It is the amount paid before any month is used: a 30 dollar fee. The 12 is the cost per month.

solve.answer: A one-time fee of 30 dollars is paid at the start.
solve.work: 30 is the intercept: cost at x=0, a starting fee.

questions.skill: Find the input for a given prediction
questions.stem: Water is added to a tank. The model $y = 5x + 20$ gives the liters $y$ in the tank after $x$ minutes. After how many minutes does the model predict 70 liters?
questions.solution: Set $5x + 20 = 70$. Subtract 20 to get $5x = 50$, so $x = 10$ minutes.

questions.skill: Predict with the model
questions.stem: The model $y = 6x + 4$ gives the total points $y$ a player has scored after $x$ games. How many points does the model predict after 5 games?
questions.solution: $6 \times 5 + 4 = 30 + 4 = 34$ points.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope
questions.stem: The height $y$, in centimeters, of a burning candle is modeled by $y = -2x + 20$, where $x$ is the number of hours burned. By how many centimeters does the model say the candle gets shorter each hour?
questions.solution: The slope is $-2$: the height changes by $-2$ centimeters each hour, so the candle gets 2 centimeters shorter each hour.

solve.work: Slope -2: height falls 2 cm per hour.

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept
questions.stem: The model $y = 3x + 8$ gives the number of stickers $y$ in Rosa's collection after $x$ days. How many stickers does the model say she has at the start, when $x = 0$?
questions.solution: Put 0 in place of $x$: $3 \times 0 + 8 = 8$ stickers. This is the intercept.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope
questions.stem: The model $y = -5x + 60$ gives the liters $y$ left in a barrel after $x$ minutes of draining. What does the $-5$ tell you?
choices: The barrel gains 5 liters every minute.
The barrel loses 5 liters every minute.
The barrel is empty after 5 minutes.
questions.answer: The barrel loses 5 liters every minute.
questions.solution: The slope is $-5$. A negative slope means the amount goes down: 5 liters less for each minute.

solve.answer: The barrel loses 5 liters every minute.
solve.work: Slope -5 L per minute: loses 5 L each minute.

questions.skill: Find the input for a given prediction
questions.stem: A model is $y = 4x + 2$. For which value of $x$ does the model predict $y = 18$?
questions.solution: Solve $4x + 2 = 18$. Subtract 2: $4x = 16$. Divide by 4: $x = 4$.

questions.skill: Change in the prediction for a change in the input
questions.stem: A line of fit is $y = 3x + 1$. How much greater is the predicted $y$ when $x = 6$ than when $x = 2$?
questions.solution: At $x = 6$ the line predicts 19 and at $x = 2$ it predicts 7. The difference is $19 - 7 = 12$. (Or: 4 more units of $x$, times the slope 3, is 12.)

questions.skill: Predict with the model
questions.stem: A line of fit for a quiz score $y$ based on $x$ hours of study is $y = 4.5x + 55$. What score does the line predict for 6 hours of study?

questions.skill: Interpret the slope
questions.stem: A line of fit for students' arm span $y$ and height $x$, both in inches, is $y = 1.02x - 0.8$. What does the slope 1.02 tell you?
choices: A student 1 inch taller is predicted to have an arm span about 1.02 inches longer.
A student 1 inch taller is predicted to have an arm span about 0.8 inches shorter.
A student with an arm span of 1 inch is predicted to be 1.02 inches tall.
A student 1.02 inches taller is predicted to have an arm span 1 inch longer.
questions.answer: A student 1 inch taller is predicted to have an arm span about 1.02 inches longer.
questions.solution: The slope is the predicted change in $y$ for each 1 unit increase in $x$. Here that is 1.02 inches of arm span for each extra inch of height.

solve.answer: A student 1 inch taller is predicted to have an arm span about 1.02 inches longer.
solve.work: Slope = change in arm span per inch of height: 1.02 in per 1 in taller.

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept
questions.stem: A line of fit for a puppy's weight $y$, in kilograms, at age $x$ weeks is $y = 0.9x + 2.5$. What does the 2.5 tell you?
choices: It predicts the puppy gains 2.5 kilograms each week.
It predicts a weight of 0.9 kilograms at age 2.5 weeks.
It predicts the puppy stops growing at 2.5 kilograms.
It predicts a weight of 2.5 kilograms at age 0 weeks.
questions.answer: It predicts a weight of 2.5 kilograms at age 0 weeks.
questions.solution: The intercept is the predicted $y$ when $x = 0$: a weight of 2.5 kilograms at age 0 weeks.

solve.answer: It predicts a weight of 2.5 kilograms at age 0 weeks.

questions.skill: Find the input for a given prediction
questions.stem: A phone's battery level is modeled by $y = -4x + 100$, where $y$ is the percent left after $x$ hours of use. After how many hours does the model predict 40 percent left?
questions.solution: Solve $-4x + 100 = 40$. Subtract 100: $-4x = -60$. Divide by $-4$: $x = 15$ hours.

questions.skill: Predict with the model
questions.stem: The model $y = -1.5x + 30$ gives the liters $y$ of fuel left in a boat after $x$ hours. How many liters does it predict are left after 8 hours?

questions.skill: Interpret the slope
questions.stem: A line of fit predicts a cost of 35 dollars for 3 hours of tutoring and 55 dollars for 7 hours. By how many dollars does the predicted cost go up for each extra hour?
questions.solution: The cost rises $55 - 35 = 20$ dollars over $7 - 3 = 4$ hours. That is $20 \div 4 = 5$ dollars per hour, the slope.

questions.skill: Find the input for a given prediction
questions.stem: A line of fit is $y = 2.5x + 10$. For which value of $x$ does it predict $y = 85$?
questions.solution: Solve $2.5x + 10 = 85$. Subtract 10: $2.5x = 75$. Divide by 2.5: $x = 30$.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope
questions.stem: A line of fit for a used car's value $y$, in thousands of dollars, and its age $x$, in years, is $y = -1.8x + 22$. What does the $-1.8$ tell you?
choices: Each extra year of age raises the predicted value by 1.8 thousand dollars.
A brand-new car is predicted to be worth 1.8 thousand dollars.
Each extra year of age lowers the predicted value by 1.8 thousand dollars.
A car is predicted to lose all of its value after 1.8 years.
questions.answer: Each extra year of age lowers the predicted value by 1.8 thousand dollars.
questions.solution: The slope is negative, so the predicted value goes down as age goes up. Each extra year lowers it by 1.8 thousand dollars.

solve.answer: Each extra year of age lowers the predicted value by 1.8 thousand dollars.
solve.work: Slope -1.8 thousand per year: value drops 1.8 thousand each year.

questions.skill: Change in the prediction for a change in the input
questions.stem: The model $y = -2.5x + 80$ gives the grams $y$ of salt left in a shaker after $x$ days. What is the change in the predicted amount when $x$ goes up by 6 days? Use a negative number for a decrease.
questions.solution: Each day changes the amount by the slope, $-2.5$ grams. Over 6 days: $-2.5 \times 6 = -15$ grams.

questions.skill: Predict with the model
questions.stem: The model $y = 0.75x + 1.5$ gives the cost $y$, in dollars, of a ride of $x$ miles. What cost does it predict for a ride of 10 miles?

questions.skill: Change in the prediction for a change in the input
questions.stem: A line of fit is $y = 3.5x + 12$, where $x$ is hours of practice and $y$ is the predicted score. How many more hours of practice does the line say are needed to raise the predicted score by 14 points?
questions.solution: Each extra hour raises the predicted score by the slope, 3.5 points. To gain 14 points: $14 \div 3.5 = 4$ hours.

questions.skill: Find the input for a given prediction
questions.stem: A trainer's fees follow $y = 15x + 25$, where $y$ is the total cost in dollars and $x$ is the number of sessions. Jo has 205 dollars to spend. How many sessions does the model say Jo can pay for?
questions.solution: Solve $15x + 25 = 205$. Subtract 25: $15x = 180$. Divide by 15: $x = 12$ sessions.

questions.skill: Compare two linear models
questions.stem: Two plants are modeled for their first 10 weeks, with $h$ the height in centimeters and $x$ the weeks. Plant A: $h = 1.2x + 4$. Plant B: $h = 0.8x + 7$. At 10 weeks, how many centimeters taller does the model say Plant A is than Plant B?
questions.solution: Plant A: $1.2 \times 10 + 4 = 16$. Plant B: $0.8 \times 10 + 7 = 15$. A is $16 - 15 = 1$ centimeter taller.

questions.skill: Find the input for a given prediction
questions.stem: The model $y = -2.4x + 96$ gives the gallons $y$ in a tank after $x$ hours of draining. After how many hours does the model predict the tank is empty?
questions.solution: The tank is empty when $y = 0$. Solve $-2.4x + 96 = 0$: $2.4x = 96$, so $x = 40$ hours.

questions.skill: Change in the prediction for a change in the input
questions.stem: In the model $y = 0.07x + 1.2$, $y$ is the liters of fuel a car has used and $x$ is the kilometers it has driven. The car drives 100 more kilometers. By how much does the model say the fuel used goes up?
choices: The fuel used goes up by 0.07 liters.
The fuel used goes up by 8.2 liters.
The fuel used goes up by 70 liters.
The fuel used goes up by 7 liters.
questions.answer: The fuel used goes up by 7 liters.
questions.solution: The slope 0.07 is liters per kilometer. For 100 more kilometers: $0.07 \times 100 = 7$ liters. The 1.2 is not added again, because it is only the starting value.

solve.answer: The fuel used goes up by 7 liters.

questions.skill: Interpret the intercept
questions.stem: A line of fit for children aged 5 to 12 is $y = 6x + 78$, where $x$ is age in years and $y$ is height in centimeters. Which statement about the 78 is correct?
choices: At age 5 it predicts 78 cm, the youngest age in the data.
At age 0 it predicts 78 cm, outside the data, so it is unreliable.
Each year of age adds 78 cm to the predicted height.
At age 12 it predicts 78 cm, the oldest age in the data.
questions.answer: At age 0 it predicts 78 cm, outside the data, so it is unreliable.
questions.solution: The 78 is the intercept, the prediction at $x = 0$. The data only cover ages 5 to 12, so age 0 is far outside them and the prediction is not reliable.

solve.answer: At age 0 it predicts 78 cm, outside the data, so it is unreliable.
solve.work: 78 is the value at x=0, outside ages 5-12, so extrapolation. Age 5 gives 108, age 12 gives 150, so A and D false; C is the slope misread.

questions.skill: Predict with the model
questions.stem: A model for the cost $y$, in dollars, of a repair is $y = 12x + 40$, where $x$ is the number of hours of labor. What cost does the model predict for 90 minutes of labor?
questions.solution: 90 minutes is 1.5 hours. $12 \times 1.5 + 40 = 18 + 40 = 58$ dollars.

questions.skill: Find the input for a given prediction
questions.stem: The value of a machine is modeled by $y = -450x + 9{,}000$, where $y$ is its value in dollars after $x$ years. After how many years does the model predict the value is half of the starting value?
questions.solution: The starting value is 9,000, so half is 4,500. Solve $-450x + 9000 = 4500$: $-450x = -4500$, so $x = 10$ years.

questions.skill: Predict with the model
questions.stem: The line of fit $y = 0.5x - 4$ predicts the profit $y$, in dollars, of a lemonade stand that sells $x$ cups. What profit does it predict for 18 cups?
questions.solution: $0.5 \times 18 = 9$, and $9 - 4 = 5$ dollars.

questions.skill: Compare two linear models
questions.stem: Two phone plans have total cost $y$, in dollars, after $x$ months. Plan A: $y = 4x + 10$. Plan B: $y = 6x + 2$. Which statement is true?
choices: Plan B rises faster, and Plan A costs more at the start.
Plan A rises faster, and Plan B costs more at the start.
Plan B rises faster, and Plan B costs more at the start.
Plan A rises faster, and Plan A costs more at the start.
questions.answer: Plan B rises faster, and Plan A costs more at the start.
questions.solution: Compare slopes: B has 6 dollars per month and A has 4, so B rises faster. Compare intercepts: A starts at 10 dollars and B at 2, so A costs more at the start.

solve.answer: Plan B rises faster, and Plan A costs more at the start.
solve.work: Slopes 4 vs 6: B rises faster. Intercepts 10 vs 2: A costs more at start.

questions.skill: Read counts and totals from a two-way table
questions.stem: A survey asked students how they get to school. Grade 7: 10 walk and 20 ride the bus. Grade 8: 14 walk and 16 ride the bus. How many Grade 8 students were surveyed?
questions.solution: Add the Grade 8 row: 14 walk and 16 ride the bus, so 14 + 16 = 30 students.

questions.skill: Complete a two-way table
questions.stem: A survey of 45 students sorted answers by grade and by whether the student likes soccer. There are 25 students in Grade 7, and 17 of them like soccer. How many Grade 7 students do not like soccer?
questions.solution: The Grade 7 row total is 25. Take away the 17 who like soccer: 25 - 17 = 8.

questions.skill: Relative frequency from a two-way table
questions.stem: In a survey, 25 Grade 7 students were asked which pet they prefer. 15 of them prefer dogs and 10 prefer cats. What fraction of the Grade 7 students prefer dogs? Write your answer as a decimal.
questions.solution: The relative frequency is 15 out of the 25 Grade 7 students: 15/25 = 3/5 = 0.6.

questions.skill: Construct a two-way table from data
questions.stem: Ten students were asked their grade and whether they have a phone. The answers, as (grade, phone?), were: (7, yes), (7, yes), (7, no), (8, yes), (8, yes), (8, yes), (7, no), (8, no), (7, yes), (8, yes). When the answers are sorted into a two-way table, how many Grade 8 students have a phone?
questions.solution: Go through the list and count the Grade 8 students whose answer is yes. There are 4: the 4th, 5th, 6th and 10th answers.

questions.skill: Describe association using relative frequencies
questions.stem: In a survey, 30% of the Grade 7 students and 30% of the Grade 8 students said they own a bike. What does this suggest?
choices: There is no association between grade and owning a bike.
Grade 8 students are more likely to own a bike than Grade 7 students.
Grade 7 students are more likely to own a bike than Grade 8 students.
Owning a bike depends on a student's grade in this survey.
questions.answer: There is no association between grade and owning a bike.
questions.solution: The relative frequencies are equal for the two grades, so knowing a student's grade tells us nothing about whether they own a bike. There is no association.

solve.answer: There is no association between grade and owning a bike.
solve.work: Same relative frequency (30%) in both grades, so no association.

questions.skill: Read counts and totals from a two-way table
questions.stem: In a two-way table the row totals are 24 and 36. The column totals are 30 and 30. How many people are in the table altogether?
questions.solution: The grand total is the sum of the row totals: 24 + 36 = 60. The column totals also add to 30 + 30 = 60.

solve.work: Grand total = sum of row totals = 24 + 36 = 60 = 30 + 30.

questions.skill: Complete a two-way table
questions.stem: A two-way table sorts 40 students by grade and by whether they like the new lunch menu. Grade 7: 14 say yes and ? say no, with 20 students in all. Grade 8: 9 say yes and 11 say no. What number is the ?
questions.solution: The Grade 7 row must add to 20. Since 14 said yes, the number who said no is 20 - 14 = 6.

questions.skill: Relative frequency from a two-way table
questions.stem: Of the 80 students surveyed, 20 are Grade 8 students who walk to school. What percent of all the students surveyed are Grade 8 students who walk?
questions.solution: The joint relative frequency is 20 out of 80 = 1/4 = 25%.

questions.skill: Construct a two-way table from data
questions.stem: A survey records each student's grade (7 or 8) and favorite season. How should these data be organized in a two-way table?
choices: Put one category in the rows and the other in the columns, and add the ages of the students.
Put the students' names in the rows and leave the columns empty, with no counts.
Put each category on its own number line and mark one dot for each student.
Put one category in the rows and the other in the columns, and count the students in each pair.
questions.answer: Put one category in the rows and the other in the columns, and count the students in each pair.
questions.solution: A two-way table has one categorical variable in the rows and the other in the columns. Each cell counts the students who fall in both categories.

solve.answer: Put one category in the rows and the other in the columns, and count the students in each pair.
solve.work: A two-way table puts one categorical variable in rows, the other in columns, and counts each pair.

questions.skill: Read counts and totals from a two-way table
questions.stem: In a survey of 60 students, the boys gave these answers: 18 like math and 12 do not. The girls: 15 like math and 15 do not. How many of the students surveyed like math?
questions.solution: Add the "like math" counts of the two rows: 18 + 15 = 33.

questions.skill: Complete a two-way table
questions.stem: A survey of 100 students sorted the answers by grade and by whether the student likes music. There are 55 students in Grade 7, and 28 of them like music. In all, 60 students like music. How many Grade 8 students like music?
questions.solution: The 60 students who like music are split between the grades. Grade 7 has 28 of them, so Grade 8 has 60 - 28 = 32.

solve.work: Music total 60, Grade 7 music 28; Grade 8 music = 60 - 28 = 32.

questions.skill: Complete a two-way table
questions.stem: A club has 90 members: 50 girls and the rest boys. 35 of the boys and 20 of the girls play an instrument. How many of the members do not play an instrument?
questions.solution: 35 + 20 = 55 members play an instrument, so 90 - 55 = 35 do not.

solve.work: Boys = 90 - 50 = 40. Play: 35 + 20 = 55. Do not play: 90 - 55 = 35 (boys 5, girls 30).

questions.skill: Relative frequency from a two-way table
questions.stem: Grade 7: 18 students text every day and 12 do not. Grade 8: 21 students text every day and 9 do not. What percent of the Grade 8 students text every day?
questions.solution: Grade 8 has 21 + 9 = 30 students. The relative frequency is 21/30 = 0.7, which is 70%.

questions.skill: Relative frequency from a two-way table
questions.stem: Students were asked how they get to school. Bus: 24 in Grade 7 and 16 in Grade 8. Walk: 6 in Grade 7 and 14 in Grade 8. Of the students who walk, what fraction are in Grade 7?
questions.solution: The walk column has 6 + 14 = 20 students, and 6 of them are in Grade 7: 6/20 = 3/10. The other fractions use the wrong total: 6/60, 6/30, and the Grade 8 share 14/20.

questions.skill: Describe association using relative frequencies
questions.stem: Grade 7: 15 students own a phone and 10 do not. Grade 8: 20 students own a phone and 5 do not. By how many percentage points is the percent of Grade 8 students who own a phone greater than the percent of Grade 7 students who do?
questions.solution: Grade 8: 20/25 = 80%. Grade 7: 15/25 = 60%. The difference is 80 - 60 = 20 percentage points.

questions.skill: Construct a two-way table from data
questions.stem: Twelve students gave their grade and the pet they prefer, in this order: 7-dog, 8-cat, 7-cat, 7-dog, 8-dog, 8-cat, 7-cat, 8-dog, 7-dog, 8-cat, 7-dog, 8-cat. What fraction of the Grade 7 students prefer dogs?
questions.solution: Sort the answers: Grade 7 has 4 dog and 2 cat answers, 6 students in all. So 4/6 = 2/3 of the Grade 7 students prefer dogs.

solve.work: Grade 7 entries: dog, cat, dog, cat, dog, dog -> 6 students, 4 dog. 4/6 = 2/3.

questions.skill: Read counts and totals from a two-way table
questions.stem: Small items: 12 red, 9 blue and 4 green. Large items: 8 red, 15 blue and 7 green. How many more large items than small items are there?
questions.solution: Large: 8 + 15 + 7 = 30. Small: 12 + 9 + 4 = 25. The difference is 30 - 25 = 5.

questions.skill: Describe association using relative frequencies
questions.stem: Students who study with music: 24 passed a test and 6 failed. Students who study without music: 30 passed and 70 failed. Which statement describes the association?
choices: Students who study without music pass more often, because 30 of them passed and only 24 of the others did.
There is no association, because some students in each group passed and some failed the test.
Students who study with music pass more often: 80% of them passed, compared with 30% of the others.
Students who study with music pass more often because they are the smaller group of the two.
questions.answer: Students who study with music pass more often: 80% of them passed, compared with 30% of the others.
questions.solution: With music: 24 of 30 passed, which is 80%. Without music: 30 of 100 passed, which is 30%. Comparing percents, not counts, shows the association. The groups differ in size, so counts are misleading.

solve.answer: Students who study with music pass more often: 80% of them passed, compared with 30% of the others.
solve.work: With music: 24/30 = 80% pass. Without: 30/100 = 30% pass. Option with 80% vs 30%.

questions.skill: Complete a two-way table
questions.stem: A table has 100 people in all. Row A has 60 people, and the Yes column has 45. The cell for row A and Yes holds 28. How many people are in the cell for row B and No?
questions.solution: Row B has 100 - 60 = 40 people. The cell for B and Yes is 45 - 28 = 17. So B and No holds 40 - 17 = 23.

questions.skill: Relative frequency from a two-way table
questions.stem: A survey of 200 students found 90 in Grade 7 and 110 who prefer tea. 36 students are in Grade 7 and prefer tea. What fraction of all the students surveyed are Grade 7 students who prefer tea?
questions.solution: The question asks about all 200 students, so the denominator is 200. The joint relative frequency is 36/200. The others use a row total, a column total, or a different group.

solve.work: Joint relative frequency: 36 out of all 200 = 36/200.

questions.skill: Complete a two-way table
questions.stem: A school surveyed 200 students. 60% are girls. 3/4 of the girls and 1/2 of the boys have a library card. How many of the students in all have a library card?
questions.solution: Girls: 60% of 200 = 120, so there are 80 boys. Cards: 3/4 of 120 = 90 girls and 1/2 of 80 = 40 boys. In all 90 + 40 = 130.

questions.skill: Relative frequency from a two-way table
questions.stem: Under 18: 45 recycle and 15 do not. Age 18 and over: 75 recycle and 65 do not. What percent of the people who recycle are 18 or over?
questions.solution: The people who recycle number 45 + 75 = 120, and 75 of them are 18 or over: 75/120 = 0.625 = 62.5%. The 53.6% is 75/140, which uses the row total.

questions.skill: Describe association using relative frequencies
questions.stem: Students who practice every day: 42 passed an exam and 18 failed. Students who do not practice every day: 30 passed and 70 failed. By how many percentage points does the pass rate of the daily practicers exceed the pass rate of the others?
questions.solution: Daily: 42/60 = 70%. Others: 30/100 = 30%. The difference is 70 - 30 = 40 percentage points.

questions.skill: Describe association using relative frequencies
questions.stem: A school asked 60 Grade 7 students and 120 Grade 8 students about a new schedule. In Grade 7, 30 said yes and 30 said no. In Grade 8, 60 said yes and 60 said no. A student says: "Grade 8 likes the schedule more, because 60 is more than 30." Which response is correct?
choices: The claim is right, because Grade 8 has twice as many students who said yes.
The claim is wrong: Grade 7 likes it more, since fewer Grade 7 students said no.
The claim is wrong: half of each grade said yes, so there is no association.
The claim is right: Grade 8 has more students, so its answers should count more.
questions.answer: The claim is wrong: half of each grade said yes, so there is no association.
questions.solution: Compare relative frequencies: 30/60 = 50% in Grade 7 and 60/120 = 50% in Grade 8. They are equal, so there is no association. The counts differ only because the grades differ in size.

solve.answer: The claim is wrong: half of each grade said yes, so there is no association.
solve.work: Grade 7: 30/60 = 50% yes; Grade 8: 60/120 = 50% yes. Same rate -> no association; claim wrong.

questions.skill: Construct a two-way table from data
questions.stem: Nine students were asked their grade and how they get to school. In order: Grade 7 bus, Grade 7 walk, Grade 8 bus, Grade 7 bus, Grade 8 walk, Grade 8 bus, Grade 7 bus, Grade 8 bus, Grade 7 walk. Which two-way table matches the answers?
choices: Grade 7: 2 bus, 3 walk; Grade 8: 3 bus, 1 walk
Grade 7: 3 bus, 2 walk; Grade 8: 1 bus, 3 walk
Grade 7: 4 bus, 1 walk; Grade 8: 3 bus, 1 walk
Grade 7: 3 bus, 2 walk; Grade 8: 3 bus, 1 walk
questions.answer: Grade 7: 3 bus, 2 walk; Grade 8: 3 bus, 1 walk
questions.solution: Tally each answer. Grade 7 bus: 1st, 4th and 7th = 3. Grade 7 walk: 2nd and 9th = 2. Grade 8 bus: 3rd, 6th and 8th = 3. Grade 8 walk: 5th = 1.

solve.answer: Grade 7: 3 bus, 2 walk; Grade 8: 3 bus, 1 walk
solve.work: Grade 7: bus, walk, bus, bus, walk -> 3 bus, 2 walk. Grade 8: bus, walk, bus, bus -> 3 bus, 1 walk. Total 9.

questions.skill: Relative frequency from a two-way table
questions.stem: In a survey of 250 people, the relative frequency of people who are over 40 and prefer tea is 0.18. How many people are over 40 and prefer tea?
questions.solution: A relative frequency is the count divided by the total, so the count is 0.18 x 250 = 45.

questions.skill: Complete a two-way table
questions.stem: Of 150 students, 90 are in Grade 8. The "yes" column total is 100, and 55 Grade 8 students said yes. How many Grade 7 students said no?
questions.solution: Grade 7 has 150 - 90 = 60 students. Grade 7 yes = 100 - 55 = 45. So Grade 7 no = 60 - 45 = 15.

questions.skill: Describe association using relative frequencies
questions.stem: Which table shows no association between grade and answering yes?
choices: Grade 7: 25 yes, 25 no; Grade 8: 25 yes, 75 no
Grade 7: 20 yes, 30 no; Grade 8: 40 yes, 60 no
Grade 7: 20 yes, 30 no; Grade 8: 30 yes, 40 no
Grade 7: 20 yes, 30 no; Grade 8: 60 yes, 40 no
questions.answer: Grade 7: 20 yes, 30 no; Grade 8: 40 yes, 60 no
questions.solution: No association means the relative frequencies match. In the first table 20/50 = 40% and 40/100 = 40%. In the others the percents differ: 50% and 25%, 40% and about 43%, 40% and 60%.

solve.answer: Grade 7: 20 yes, 30 no; Grade 8: 40 yes, 60 no

questions.skill: Describe association using relative frequencies
questions.stem: Of 80 students who eat breakfast, 64 are on time for first period. Of 20 students who skip breakfast, 10 are on time. Which statement best describes the association?
choices: Students who skip breakfast are more likely to be on time: 50% compared with 20%.
There is no association, because both groups have students who are on time.
Students who eat breakfast are more likely to be on time: 80% compared with 50%.
Students who skip breakfast are more likely to be on time, since only 20 of them were surveyed.
questions.answer: Students who eat breakfast are more likely to be on time: 80% compared with 50%.
questions.solution: Breakfast: 64/80 = 80% on time. No breakfast: 10/20 = 50% on time. The higher percent is for the breakfast group, so eating breakfast is associated with being on time.

solve.answer: Students who eat breakfast are more likely to be on time: 80% compared with 50%.

questions.skill: Construct a two-way table from data
questions.stem: A coach records 50 athletes: 30 are runners and the rest are swimmers. 18 of the runners and 9 of the swimmers wear a team jacket. How many of the athletes do not wear a jacket?
questions.solution: There are 50 - 30 = 20 swimmers. Jackets: 18 + 9 = 27. So 50 - 27 = 23 do not wear a jacket.
